entries.reason: iOS 6 has no +contextWithCGContext: in either spelling - the 6.1.3 selector table has contextWithOptions:, contextWithEAGLContext: and contextWithEAGLContext:options: and nothing to extend - so the context here is one of the release's own, made by the release's own method, with the drawing surface beside it
entries.effect: a context of the release's own, made with the release's own +contextWithOptions:, that draws into the CGContext named; a category cannot add storage to a class the framework has, so the surface is an associated object on the context
entries.source: the header of the iOS 16.4 SDK for the contract; the host's own CoreImage over the same calls, by tests/backports/host/ciimage/pixel, which draws into a CGContext on both sides and prints the bytes that context ended up holding; the 6.1.3 armv7 selector table for what the release has

entries.reason: iOS 6 has no primitive that takes a properties dictionary and makes an image, and the method is missing from the release; the row is carried as a crutch and coordination/crutches.md records what it answers and what it cannot
entries.effect: the image's own properties plus the caller's, on a copy of the image; the values read back correctly, and the copy is the image on the system measured here, so the measurement that cannot match is that the system's answer is a distinct object of the same extent
entries.source: the host's own CoreImage over the same call, by tests/backports/host/ciimage/pixel, which prints the identity, the class and the extent of what came back; the two-process probe's values and pixels for the row

entries.reason: iOS 6 has no filter that divides by alpha - CIDivideBlendMode is absent from its 6.1.3 cache and it has no kernel it can compile one from - and the method is missing from the release, so the arithmetic is the port's own over the rendered bytes and the row is a crutch
entries.effect: each colour channel divided by the alpha in float, the alpha untouched, a result over one clamped, and an infinite extent answered as the image itself, which is what the system does; one unit of 255 out on a channel, and a premultiply followed by an unpremultiply is not the identity as it is on the system
entries.source: the host's own CoreImage over the same call, by tests/backports/host/ciimage/pixel, which prints the rendered bytes and four pixels of them and the round trip's checksum; coordination/crutches.md for what is still open
